description:
A series of mausolea from a large late Roman Cemetery just outside of the Roman town of Durnovaria. The cemetery originates in the late Iron Age or early Roman period, though there is a single neonate burial associated with a late Bronze Age structure. From at least the late 3rd CE we see seven mausolea of varying sizes containing between 2 and 7 graves each, as well as three ditched funerary enclosures.

These mausolea have been compared with similar contemporary structures considered 'shrine-like' and associated with both burials and temples at Brean Down, Lamyatt Beacon, Maiden Castle, and Nettleton Scrubb. It is also compared with early Christian chapels and shrines at Icklingham and Ardwall Island. 

It might be best to consider these mausolea as potentially a type of funerary shrine, this interpretation does not seem to be extended to the ditched funerary enclosures, though very similar funerary structures have been interpreted as shrines in different contests, Rhynie for example.

By the late 4th CE the mausolea seem to have fallen into disuse, coins dating from this period and earlier were found beneath collapsed building roof material. The cemetery continued to be used, though with to a lesser extent, in the post-Roman period.
bibliography: Farewell, and Molleson. “Excavations at Poundbury 1966-1980.” Dorset Natural History and Archaeological Society Monograph Series, 11, 2 (1993).
Sparey Green. “Excavations at Poundbury 1966-1982.” Natural History and Archaeological Society Monograph Series, 7, 1 (1987).
